narration: Here are five Chrome DevTools features I use every single day. Let me show you what they do.

shots.desc: DevTools demo app loaded in browser
5 DevTools Tricks Every Developer Should Know

narration: You don't need to edit your source files just to test a design change. Open the Elements panel, find the CSS rule, and change the value directly. Watch — I'll change the border radius from twelve pixels to thirty-two. The page updates instantly. No save, no reload, no build step.

shots.desc: Demo app with cards at 12px border-radius
Cursor moves to Styles panel, border-radius field

narration: The Console isn't just for reading logs. It's a live JavaScript REPL. You can run any code against the current page. For example, I can grab the title element and change its text right here. The page updates immediately. No editor required.

shots.desc: Demo app with original title 'DevTools Demo'

narration: If an API call fails, the Network panel tells you exactly what happened. I'll click Load Users, which fetches data from a local API. The request appears here. Click it, and you can see the headers that were sent, the response body, and the timing breakdown. Everything you need to debug a failed request.

shots.desc: Demo app with empty user list
Highlight the /api/users request in Network panel
Zoom to Headers tab showing request/response headers
Zoom to Response tab showing JSON body
Return to page showing 6 loaded user cards

narration: Want to test how your app handles no internet? The Network panel has a throttling dropdown. Set it to Offline, reload the page, and you can see exactly what happens when the connection drops. The page fails to load, and you can debug the error handling — all without pulling your ethernet cable.

shots.desc: Highlight the throttling dropdown in Network panel

narration: Testing responsive design doesn't require a pile of phones. Toggle the Device Toolbar, and you can simulate any viewport size. Watch the navbar collapse and the layout reflow as I switch from desktop to a mobile width. You can test breakpoints instantly.

shots.desc: Highlight the Device Toolbar toggle button
Click toggle to enable Device Mode

narration: Those are five DevTools features that save me time every day. Live CSS editing, the Console as a REPL, Network inspection, offline testing, and Device Mode. Try them in your next project.
